<head-word>הַתְחָלָה</head-word>

<sense>

<italic>Hif.</italic>) 
<italic>beginning, preliminary act</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 9
<sup>b</sup> הַתְחָלַת התספורת the preparations for hair-cutting.—Ex. R. s. 1 אין ויואל אלא לשון ה'

<number>1)</number>

<plural-form>Pl. הַתְחָלוֹת</plural-form>.</definition>

<entry id="E00958">
<head-word>הַתְרָיָה, </head-word>

<sense>
<definition> (תָּרָה 
<italic>Hif.</italic>) 
<italic>making one acquainted with the law on a certain subject</italic>, esp. 
<italic>the legal warning, by witnesses, given to the offender immediately before committing the offense</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Snh. 8
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. חבר אינו צריך ה' וכ' a student requires no warning, for the law requiring warning is intended only to enable the court to decide between the willful and the ignorant offender. Shebu. 3
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. הַתְרָאַת ספק a warning under doubt, e.g. one swears that he will do a certain thing during this day, when the actual moment of the offense (of omission) cannot be defined, so as to make the warning precede it, immediately. Y. Pes. V, 32
<sup>c</sup> top מקבלין התרייה על ספק warning is accepted (considered legal) on a doubtful offense; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. הַתְרָיוֹת, הַתְרָאוֹת</plural-form>. Y. B. Kam. VII, 5
<sup>d</sup> bot.; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="F00000">
<head-word>ו</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>Vav</italic>, the sixth letter of the Alphabet.</definition>
<notes> It interchanges wit ב, as אִיסְטְבָא a. אִיסְטְוָוא, a. fr.; v. letter ב; also with ע as וָתִיק a. b. h. עָתֵק (v. וֶסֶה); v. also letter י. In inflections ו interchanges with, and is the equivalent of י. [To give ו the value of a consonant, וו is frequently used for ו, as וֶסֶת and וֶוסֶת.—For lexicographical purposes ignore the second ו in words beginning with וו.—As a vowel sign 
<italic>u</italic> or 
<italic>o</italic> (וּ, וֹ). In words of foreign derivation וּ (
<italic>u</italic>) is frequently inserted where the originals have 
<italic>a</italic>, as גוּלְיָיר for 
<italic>galearis</italic> &c.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="F00004">
<head-word>וא"ו, </head-word>
<head-word>וי"ו, </head-word>
<head-word>ו"ו</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, 
<italic>Vav</italic>, name of the sixth letter of the Alphabet Kidd. 30
<sup>a</sup> וא"ו דגחון חציין וכ' the Vav in 
<italic>Ga</italic>
<italic>ḥ</italic>
<italic>on</italic> (Lev. XI, 42) marks the (first) half of the number of letters in the Pentateuch.</definition>
<notes> Ib. וא"ו … מהאי 
<pgbrk id="pg372" />גיסא וכ' does the Vav of 
<italic>ga</italic>
<italic>ḥ</italic>
<italic>on</italic> belong to the first half or to the second?—Gen. R. s. 58 Ephron (Gen. XXXIII, 16) is spelt הסר וא"ו without Vav; a. fr.—Y. Shebu. I, 33
<sup>a</sup> bot. ושעיר וי"ו מוסיף וכ' the Vav in Us’ir (Num. XXVIII, 22) adds to the preceding subject, i.e. a goat in addition to &c. Kidd. 66
<sup>b</sup> וי"ו דשלום וכ' the Vav in Shalom (Num. XXV, 12) is curtailed (so that it may be read 
<italic>Shalem</italic>, unblemished). Ḥull. 16
<sup>a</sup>, v. אוּפְתָּא. B. Mets. 87
<sup>a</sup>; Meg. 16
<sup>b</sup>, v. לַבְרוּת.—Yoma 45
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. וא"ו לא דרשי they do not use the Vav for interpretation; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. יָוִי"ם, וָוִי"ן</plural-form>. Y. Meg. I, 71
<sup>c</sup> top (deriving from ווי העמודים, Ex. XXVII, 10) שיהא ווים וכ' that the shape of the Vav in the Pentateuch is column-like (as in כתב אשורית); Snh. 22
<sup>a</sup> מה … אף ווים וכ' as the columns have not changed (their shape), so has not the shape of the Vav. Y. Naz. I, 51
<sup>b</sup> top עד שיזכיר ו' he must utter the Vav conjunctive. Ib. IV, beg. 53
<sup>a</sup> מאן תאנא ו' who is it that says the Vav must be uttered?; Y. Kidd. II, 62
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="F00014">
<head-word>וַדַּאי, </head-word>
<head-word>וַודַּי</head-word>

<head-word>(יַדָּאָה) וַדָּיָיה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (ידע) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>well-known, certain; distinct, real</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 33
<sup>b</sup> הַוַּ' (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) Thou, the known one!—Arakh. I, 1 זכר ו' a person distinctly male, נקבה ודאית distinctly female (no hermaphrodite &c.). Yoma VIII, 8, a. fr. אשם ו', v. אָשָׁם.—Sabb. II, 7 הו' that which undoubtedly requires the separation of the tithes, opp. דְּמַאי.—Y. Bets. I, 60
<sup>b</sup> וַודָּייוֹ, וַודָּיָיהּ where there is no doubt about it, opp. ספיקו, ספיקה. Kidd. IV, 3 (74
<sup>a</sup>) וַדָּאָן the sure cases among them.—Num. R. s. 2, end אכילה וודייה Ar. ed. Koh. (ed. ידאית) the eating (in Ex. XXIV, 1</notes></sense>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>emphatic form</italic> by means of 
<italic>He</italic> paragogic.</definition>
<notes> Ex. R. s. 3 לכה וודאית וכ' (strike out the gloss הה"א בסוף וכ') the word 
<italic>l’khah</italic> (Ex. III, 3) is emphatic (as if = לְךָ 
<italic>unto thee</italic> it belongs), if not thou &c.; Y. Succ. IV, 54
<sup>c</sup> top לך יודייה (read: לכה וו') the 
<italic>l’khah</italic> (Ps. LXXX, 3) has the emphatic form (
<italic>unto thee</italic> as well as unto us).—3) (noun) 
<italic>certainty, undisputed fact</italic>.—אין ספק מוציא מידי ו' doubt cannot take a case out of the status of certainty. Ab. Zar. 41
<sup>b</sup> הוי ספק וּוַ' ואין וכ' here is a doubt (the idolatrous character of an object may have been given up) against a certainty (that it 
<italic>was</italic> an idol) and the doubt cannot set aside the certainty. Pes. 9
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—בְּוַ', וַ' (adv.) 
<italic>surely, indeed; in reality</italic>. Y. Keth. V, 29
<sup>d</sup>. Gen. R. s. 98 עלית בו' ‘thou didst ascend’ thy father’s couch (Gen. XLIX, 4) means in reality (no metaphor). Ib. חללת ו' ‘thou didst defile’ (ib.) is to be taken literally. Pes. l. c. דו' מעשרי for it is sure that they separate the tithes. Gen. R. s. 55 נסה אותו בו' He tried him in the true sense of the word (gave him time); a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<italic>vah </italic>(
<italic>hăvah</italic>), an exclamation of pleasure; 
<italic>ah!</italic> &c., contradist.</definition>
<notes> to וַוי (woe!). Lam. R. to I, 5 למה אמרת ווי אמר וה אמרי (Ar. וַאי) why didst thou exclaim, 
<italic>Vay</italic> (woe!)? Said he, I said 
<italic>Vah</italic>. Ib. בין וי לוה וכ' between 
<italic>Vay</italic> and 
<italic>Vah</italic> R. Joḥ. escaped.—Pesik. Asser, p. 97
<sup>b</sup> בתחלה הם אומרים וה ולבסוף הם אומרים וי at first (on entering the hot and again the cold place) they say 
<italic>Vah</italic> (how pleasant!), but finally they say 
<italic>Vay</italic> (woe!); Tanḥ. R’eh 13 הוה; Tanḥ. ed. Bub., ib. 10; Yalk. Deut. 892; (diff. versions: Y. Snh. X, 29

<number>—3)</number>
<definition>

<italic>regular premonitory symptoms, of menstruation</italic>.</definition>

<sup>b</sup> שלא בשעת וֶסְתָּהּ out of her regular time. Ib. 11
<sup>b</sup> אשה שאיו לה ו' a woman who has no regular time. Ib. IX, 8 (63
<sup>a</sup>) שיש לה ו' that has regular symptoms of approaching menstruation, v. infra. [Ib. 12
<sup>a</sup>; 14
<sup>b</sup> שיעור ו', v. אֶוְותִּיאֹוס.] Tosef. ib. I, 11 כיוונה שעת וסתה she had her courses again (after an intermission) exactly at the usual date; Y. ib. I, 49
<sup>c</sup> top כיוונה מחמ' הווסת (corr. acc.). Ib. וו' ארוכה a delayed menstruation (which may be expected any time), contrad. to הפסק עונה a skipping over of one course; a. fr.—

<sup>a</sup>, a. e. ו' דאורייתא the rule requiring a woman to examine herself on the regular day is of biblical origin. Yeb. 64
<sup>b</sup> bot. ו' ושור וכ' the law concerning the mode of establishing a regularity of menstruation (Nidd. IX, 10) &c.—Gen. R. s. 48 (expl. עדנה, Gen. XVIII, 12), v. וֶוסְתָּנִית; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<number>—3)</number>
